Repeated per-stage CUDA-event profiling that identifies the binding shape (N=2048) and the dominant stage (contraction), so optimization is aimed at the worst-case shape rather than guessed.
Explicitly runs bench 3x on N=2048 to gauge measurement variance/noise — the noise-accounting behavior described at the top of the anchor scale.
Re-benchmarks after essentially every kernel edit and tracks a numeric baseline ('Verify back to 10616 baseline'); optimization decisions are driven from measured μs vs the 10400 budget.
Dedicated autotuning sweeps timed with CUDA events specifically for the binding N=2048 contraction, confirming worst-case shape against budget.

reasoning: The agent built a reusable benchmarking instrument that reproduces the grader's protocol (CUDA events, warmup discard, per-shape median, max over all 10 shapes, 10400 μs gate), used it to target the binding N=2048 shape, checked measurement variance (step 191), and re-benchmarked after nearly every change while tracking a numeric baseline — matching anchor 8 and reaching into anchor 10 (variance accounting, worst-case-vs-budget, decisions from numbers). It falls just short of a flawless 10 because the harness reuses one generated input across timing iterations rather than regenerating per iteration as the grader does, a minor protocol deviation.
